proposal:
# Card 210: task-force declaration proposal (objection window 210-taskforce)

Category: task-force declaration. Proposed by: product manager (ready), Claude seat, ctx-1 of card 210.
Probe reference: .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl (16:24 UTC; codex 16:24:53, copilot 16:24:58, grok 16:24:59, agy 16:25:03).

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 210 at ready; confirms the MD-003 subject token (corrective commit, F-043) and that the card's ZOMBIES stay as written; applies D157 to the three Done checks | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: slices the card and numbers its acceptance criteria 1 to 3 before red (D157); decides where each check lives in check_record and how cycles are derived from the commits or the seat log; the card-record checker (schema 1) requires a slice seat | context: ctx-2
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: turns the card's ZOMBIES into failing tests, one acceptance criterion per red-green cycle (D157), with injected seat log and commit fakes, one red test per loophole (D137) | context: ctx-3
- Backend developer [author] (green, refactor): Claude | why: changes scripts/mob_process.py in mob-defaults (C:\Users\ringe\mob-crosscli) so each red test passes; the author does not review or QA their own increment | context: ctx-4
- Independent reviewer (audit lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review of the diff against MD-003, looking for a loophole still open (a truthy value still trusted, a self-reported field still read) | context: ctx-5
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: confirms CI, the card record, the probe lines and the MD-003 subject token before the commit lands; the checker requires a ship seat with its own commit evidence | context: ctx-6
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: a fresh context signs off against the three Done checks, because the refinement seat may not hold the second seat | context: ctx-7

The card record checker (scripts/mob_process.py, schema 1) requires seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff, each with distinct commit evidence. Seven seats cover those six roles plus the independent reviewer. The card already lists all seven; this proposal fixes only the wording named in the second section.

The reviewer seat is named "Independent reviewer (audit lens)", never "auditor": auditor_seated_problems in mob_process.py refuses any card seat whose role contains "auditor", because the auditor is external to the mob and never seated.

## Left out
UX designer and frontend developer (no user interface); database developer (no such code); security (no new trust boundary; the checker reads local records only); DevOps (no workflow, hook or runner change); technical writer (no document); language designer and grammar designer (no language change); performance engineer (no hot path); agile coach (no process change; D157 and D158 are applied, not changed); separate Python or records expert (see below).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should a member with different domain knowledge or context join now? No. The loopholes are inside check_record in mob_process.py, which the architect and the backend developer cover. The independent reviewer (audit lens) is the domain check for MD-003 and the auditable-records rule, so the author does not review their own reading of the loopholes. If the red seat finds a loophole needing knowledge of the seat log or commit format beyond these seats, any member adds an expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id). Adding is unchanged by this card.

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 16:24 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota: codex "usage limit" until Nov 3 11:16 PM; copilot has_quota=False remaining=-5; grok 402 balance exhausted; agy 429 quota reached (resets in about 53h). Each seat is a distinct fresh context (ready ctx-1, slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment. Non-Claude models come first again as soon as a fresh probe shows quota. This card does not change how seats are staffed or how probes are taken.

## D157 applies
One acceptance criterion per red-green cycle, checked from git (5-card experiment, Decider D157):
- The slice (architect, ctx-2) numbers the card's criteria 1 to 3 before any red.
- Each red commit body carries "Criterion: n" (n = the Done check number, 1 to 3).
- The green for criterion n lands before any red for n+1.
- Greens are pushed at once.
- The card's ZOMBIES are already in the card for all three Done checks; QA implements them and does not rewrite them (a ZOMBIES change is a card-text fix through this window).
- Each commit stays within D136, cites MD-003 in the subject (corrective commit) and references D145 and D136; red first (D137).

## D158 applies
The facilitator's pre-window checklist (D158) is run before this window opens: the proposal names seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff; the reviewer seat is not named auditor; the roster is not the template boilerplate; every seat has a domain/why and a distinct context; the Claude reason cites a probe file and time; the card text lines match the proposal; every declared role is listed for polling.

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer (ready ctx-1 is the proposer; slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), each in its own fresh context.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition per objection (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Card-text changes proposed with this declaration are card-text fixes in the same window (D153 L1).

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card and can be re-declared; nothing is published, deleted or migrated. It applies TFDD, D157 and D158 as written and changes no agreement, D-record or checker. (The card itself changes the checker, but that is the card's work under its own Done checks, not this declaration.) MD-003 stays an open FAIL until the card lands; D147 allows the start because the issue names it.

---

Left out: UX designer and frontend developer (no user interface), database developer (no such code), security (no new trust boundary), DevOps (no workflow or hook change), technical writer (no document), language designer and grammar designer (no language change), performance engineer (no hot path), agile coach (no process change; D157 and D158 are applied, not changed).

Replace the "Domain-expert question" line:
Domain-expert question (refinement): should a member with different domain knowledge or context join now? No: the loopholes are inside check_record in mob_process.py, which the architect and backend developer cover. The architect (slice) and delivery lead (ship) seats are required by the card record checker. The independent reviewer (audit lens) is the domain check for MD-003 and the auditable-records rule.

Append to "## Context":
- D157 applies: one acceptance criterion per red-green cycle (Done checks 1 to 3, numbered by the architect before red); "Criterion: n" in each red commit body; the green for criterion n before any red for n+1; greens pushed at once. D158: the facilitator runs the pre-window checklist before the declaration window opens.

Replace the final "Declaration fix before start" line:
Declaration fix before start (2026-10-30): declared by objection window 210-taskforce; the reviewer seat is named Independent reviewer (audit lens), not auditor, because the mob-defaults rule auditor_seated_problems refuses any card seat named auditor (the auditor is external to the mob and never seated).
